statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail eases to 20% because the break to a new session low at 28,927.50 failed to extend and NQ has retraced about 88 points off it, while a 4.80% 10-year yield, a 5.27% 30-year and crude near $90 keep the environment stressed.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. Forecast Tail crosses the block threshold only inside the narrow 12:00-15:00 UTC window covering the ADP release, the US cash open and the Factory Orders and EIA prints, with a second single-hour checkpoint at the 21:00 UTC Broadcom results. headline: Nasdaq-100 futures retrace about 88 points off a failed break to a new session low as the 10-year eases to 4.80% and VIX slips from its high
body: NQ futures traded at 29,016.50 at 11:16 UTC, down 109.00 points or 0.37% from the 29,125.50 previous close, with a second independent quote at 29,014.00 (-0.38%). The structural change from the previous cycle is a failed downside extension. An hour ago the session low stood at 28,940.50 with price pinned close to it; since then the low has extended only to 28,927.50 and price has retraced roughly 88 points back off it, leaving the day range at 28,927.50-29,170.00. A marginal new low followed by a near-90-point bounce is the opposite of repeated extension after failed pullbacks, and it is why Tail eases to 20% from 22%. Three cross-checks keep the reading inside the watch band rather than lower. First, the US 10-year yield is 4.80%, marginally below the 4.82% carried in the previous cycle but still close to its highest since late 2023, with the 30-year at 5.27%; the repricing is stabilising at a high level rather than reversing. Second, VIX is 16.63, up 1.77% from a 16.34 close but now below the 16.82 session high, so the volatility impulse is decaying rather than building. Third, WTI is 89.65, down 0.64%, with reporting noting that Strait of Hormuz transit volumes reached their highest daily level since the conflict began, which weakens the immediate supply-disruption channel even as US-Iran hostilities continue. Against that, the prior session's breadth was uniformly negative in the parts of the market that matter most for this index, with all seven tracked semiconductors lower and a mean change of -1.06%, and only one of eight megacaps higher. That composition keeps Stress high at 72% while the observed intraday path keeps Tail at the lower edge of the watch band. The narrow danger window spans 12:00-15:00 UTC, covering the 12:15 UTC ADP release, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 and 14:30 UTC Factory Orders and EIA prints. No release scheduled for today has printed at the assessment cutoff, and no post-event structure is asserted.

lookbackSummary: The previous 24 hours opened with Tail elevated at 25% during the 1 September European session, peaking at 31% around that day's US cash open as the US-Iran escalation, the crude surge and the sovereign-yield selloff were priced in. Tail then decayed through the US afternoon and the Asian handover and has held a 20-25% band for the last twenty published hours. Stress stayed persistently high in a 69-77% range throughout. That profile describes a difficult, high-volatility environment in which retracements kept occurring rather than a sustained one-way trend. Three hourly slots have no published Claude assessment and are marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in a 20-23% band for most of the next 24 hours and lifts it above the block threshold only for the three-hour catalyst cluster from 12:00 to 15:00 UTC, covering the ADP release, the US cash open and the Factory Orders and EIA prints, with the single highest reading of 27% in the 13:00 UTC hour containing the opening auction. One further hour reaches the threshold at 21:00 UTC around the Broadcom results, where a top-weight semiconductor constituent can move the complex in a thin post-close book. Stress stays high throughout on the crude, sovereign-yield and Fed-repricing backdrop, which is structural rather than intraday, and eases only gradually through the Asian session before rebuilding into the 3 September European morning ahead of Challenger, jobless claims, ISM Services and Friday's payrolls. Confidence decays with forecast distance because no live price-path evidence exists for later windows at the assessment cutoff.
